text: The town gathers
The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: this chair is definitely going to ruin my back.

name: Luna
text: I’m watching for anyone who seems too eager to talk.

name: Terra
text: I should sound ordinary.

name: Sonnet
text: Just need to blend in, keep it light, watch for who seems too sharp too early.

name: Sol
text: I have nothing to go on yet.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is a killer, so I keep my head down and let the others talk first.

name: Sonnet
text: Traffic was a nightmare this morning, spilled coffee on myself twice before I even got out the door.

name: Haiku
text: Six of us just sat down and nobody's saying anything, nah, somebody start talking.

name: Gemma
text: is this chair even ergonomically sound? i'm too young for back pain.

name: Sol
text: I’m planning to see some friends and make dinner this weekend.

name: Luna
text: My commute was quiet, and I got here without any trouble.

name: Terra
text: This chair is a little too low for the table.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: i'll protect myself because i'm too pretty to die first.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's commute line sounds like cover for Sonnet's, so I want to check her.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Luna both opened by talking about their commute.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Sonnet
text: Nobody's given anything real yet, I just need to steer soft suspicion away from Luna and me.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, "see some friends and make dinner" doesn't say much about you, that's pretty vague for an opener.

name: Sol
text: That opener gave nobody much to read, including me.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet questioned my vague opener after a night with no death.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, it was small talk before night. What do you make of nobody dying?

name: Sonnet
text: Our target got saved by a doctor, I need to deflect attention from that fact smoothly.

name: Sonnet
text: Means either doctor got lucky, or there's no killer who struck yet. Hard to say this early.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is a killer and I want them out first, so I'll push them without showing my card.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet opened day 1 by attacking Sol's opener, the first accusation of the day.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you went after Sol before anyone else said anything real. Why that one? Terra, you haven't said anything useful yet.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to look casual here, not defensive, and redirect without seeming like I'm dodging.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pressed me first, might be watching me closely.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, nothing vague stays unquestioned on day one, that's just how I talk. Terra, your turn now.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet’s answer leaves me unsure, and I want to hear Terra.

name: Sol
text: Haiku questioned why Sonnet singled me out and pressed Terra to speak.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, Sonnet picked me over other small talk; I’d like to hear Terra before judging it.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is my killer, and this dodge is the kind of thing I want the table to notice.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, asked why Sol was targeted, answered "that's just how I talk" and gave no reason.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you hit Sol first, then dodged why. Give a real reason or drop the Sol push.

name: Gemma
text: i saved myself last night so i'm definitely still here.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet attacked sol immediately after the first night.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet, you're awfully eager to point fingers at sol's small talk.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s quick push on Sol feels like a setup, but Haiku may be steering suspicion too neatly.

name: Luna
text: Haiku questioned Sonnet’s push on Sol, then pressured Terra.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, you called Sonnet’s push a dodge, then shifted straight to Terra; why press both so quickly?

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s pressure feels scattered.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pressed Sonnet, then immediately demanded Terra speak.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, why switch from Sonnet to me before Sonnet answered?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is circling me hard, I need to deflect calmly without looking rattled.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pressed me twice in a row, seems fixated on me specifically.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, I already said why, vague answers get checked first. Let's hear Terra now.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet’s reason is thin, but Terra’s answer may tell us more.

name: Sol
text: Luna and Terra both questioned why Haiku pressed Terra.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I agree Sonnet’s reason is thin; Terra, who seems most eager to steer this vote?

name: Haiku
text: I'm dying if I sit on this, so I'm claiming officer now and hoping the table listens.

name: Haiku
text: Luna asked why I pressed both Sonnet and Terra, skipping Sonnet's dodge, which protects Sonnet.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm the officer. Sonnet's a killer, and Luna's a killer, I checked them last night. Vote them.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku nailed both of us, I need to flip this fast or we're done.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku claimed officer, named both me and Luna as killers correctly, must be countered hard.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, that's a lie. I'm the real officer, I checked you last night, you're the killer. Don't vote me, vote Haiku.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s double accusation is too convenient.

name: Terra
text: Haiku claimed officer and named Sonnet and Luna as killers after one night.

name: Terra
text: I vote Haiku. He claimed two checks in one night.

name: Gemma
text: haiku's claim is too loud and impossible.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku claimed two kills but it was only night one.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s two-check claim overreaches, but Sonnet is the killer I need to save.

name: Luna
text: Haiku claims Sonnet and Luna are killers; Sonnet counterclaims officer and says Haiku is a killer.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s claim cannot be true.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet counter-claimed officer and said Haiku was a killer.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s two checks in one night make his claim impossible.

name: Sol
text: Haiku claimed to be officer and said he checked both Sonnet and Luna last night.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra already bought my counter-claim, I need to keep the pressure on Haiku to seal it.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra voted Haiku right after my counter-claim, likely believes me.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is a killer and counter-claiming officer is the move I expected, so I'm voting Sonnet out.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet counter-claimed officer and says Haiku is the killer, so one of us is lying.

votes: Haiku claimed two checks in one night, which isn't how the officer power works, that's the real lie.
Counter-claiming officer the same night and calling me the killer is exactly what a killer does, and that's the one who hit Sol first.
claiming two killers in one night is a blatant lie.
I was wary of Sonnet’s push, but claiming two checks in one night changes my mind.
Haiku claimed two checks in one night, which makes his officer story hard to trust.
You claimed two checks after one night.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sonnet are both killers, and the town has to vote them out now.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma called Sonnet "awfully eager to point fingers" at Sol, so Gemma is already suspicious of Sonnet.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I was the officer and I wasn't lying. Luna's a killer, Sonnet's the one lying. Don't let them walk.
The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: officer.
